messages.subject_clean: [methylkit_discussion] Input tiled counts directly for DMR analysis?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
You can read the file as a data.frame make sure the format is the same as the internal format of methylKit, use stringsAsFactors=FALSE, when reading, also make sure other data slots are correct and consistent for all the files. You have to create a new methylRaw object with the new() function. an example is here:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/methylkit_discussion/new(%22methylRaw%22/methylkit_discussion/ndnXcLSBvLA/ezQHO3c0ZywJ

Then you can make a new methylRawList object,example is below:
# this creates a methlyRawList object from two methylRaw objects so the treatment vector has two elements.
# You can create a list with more elements
methylRawList=new("methylRawList",list(methylRawobj1,methylRawobj2),treatment=c(0,1 ) )

reading data faster
I recently created an experimental function mread, that should read large files faster, but it will not help with the memory. You can give it a try:
https://groups.google.com/d/msg/methylkit_discussion/na3jqfCgD1A/A440aOTHhHkJ

Best,
Altuna

messages.subject_clean: [methylkit_discussion] Methylated bases in the tile region are not apparent
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
for the CpGs that have coverage in a given tile or region, number of Cs and number of Ts are summed up. You can think of this sth like a weighted average of methylation values, weighted by coverage in this case. Looking at IGV browser for visually inspecting such regions may not yield what you expect. First, there is a summary process per tile as described above second some CpGs may not be included based on coverage and quality threshold when processing the SAM file.

Best,
Altuna

I'm using your package for RRBSeq analysis and in the near future will move to WGBSSeq.

Hi,

I am answering part of your question.

Hi everyone!
thank you Kalyan for your help. I solved my problem and was able to read in my .sam files. I realised that didn't remove the .sam header (@) in the first place, so this a simple command to do it for people who encountered the same problem:
grep -v "^@" S myfile.sam > myfile_noHead.sam

Also, after that, I had problems to make the "unite" function work. I realised working on a non-model organism, that the "|" after each scaffold names, caused a shit while reading my sam file. The size of the scaffold was then read as the base position, and read by unite as duplicated position for each line reporting the same scaffold. so this is how I fixed it:
sed 's/|/_/g' myfile_noHead.sam > myfile_noHead_Underscore.sam

This works well, but it takes some computing time in UNIX/linux, so if anyone thinks of a better way to do it, great.

>From then you can go on with the read.bismark function.

hope it helps the community!

@Kalyan: I can see from the help that read.bismark doesn't have a mc.cores option, you think that would still work? the computation time is high to read the .sam files, so I was wondering if there was a way (aside from having more cluster power...) to make it faster.

Thanks again, the google group is a great thing!

Leni
